**Naming of the Surah**

• It is called al-Falaq (The Daybreak), because it opens with mention of al-Falaq, which is the dawn (al-Subh).

**Among the Objectives of the Surah**

• Affirming the two aspects of Tawhid, namely Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (Oneness of Lordship) and Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Oneness of Divinity), by teaching the Prophet and his community and training them to seek refuge in Allah and take Him as their protector from the evils of His creation. It is He who suffices a person against the evil of every evil-doer, and who preserves him from every harm and every thing disliked.

[The Tafsir]

Say, O Messenger: I seek refuge and take protection with the Lord of the daybreak, which is the dawn.
From the evil of all created beings and their harm.
and from the evil of the night when its darkness is intense, when it enters and spreads through everything, and from the harms and evils that lie within it.
And from the evil of the women who blow upon knots tied (for sorcery), with the intent of practicing magic.
And from the evil of an envier who hates people when he envies them for the blessings Allah has bestowed upon them, wishing for those blessings to be removed from them and for harm to befall them.
